card.name: Comma after adverse event reports
card.fires_on: A comma (or "and") right after a statement that a serious adverse event was reported or occurred, where the next words qualify it as "including fatal..." or "some of which...".

modes.label: Comma before "including"
modes.description: Comma after a named adverse event that has been reported, leading into "including fatal cases".
modes.example: There have been postmarketing reports of acute pancreatitis<<,>> including fatal pancreatitis, in patients treated

modes.label: Comma before "some of which"
modes.description: Comma after a report of cases, leading into a subset that was fatal or needed surgery.
modes.example: In the postmarketing period, cases of gastrointestinal perforations have been reported<<,>> some of which were fatal.

modes.label: "and" before "some resulted"
modes.description: The word "and" after "Many of these reactions were serious", leading into "some resulted in death".
modes.example: Many of these adverse reactions were serious<< and>> some resulted in death.

card.writes: It promotes "some" and "few" words and suppresses "many", so the text goes on to name a subset of the cases.
card.plain: It marks the spot after a report of a serious side effect where the text goes on to say that some of the cases were severe or fatal.
